items.stem: What does the Elvis operator ?: do in Kotlin?

options.text: Provides a default value when the left-hand expression is null
options.rationale: Correct: a ?: b evaluates to a if non-null, otherwise b.

options.text: Force-unwraps a nullable value, throwing if null

options.rationale: A trailing ? on a type declares nullability; ?: supplies a fallback.

options.text: Calls a method only if the receiver is null
options.rationale: The safe-call ?. calls only when non-null; ?: supplies a default.

items.stem: Why prefer a Kotlin sequence over a plain list for a long chain of transformations on large data?

options.text: A sequence evaluates lazily, avoiding intermediate collections at each step
options.rationale: Correct: sequences process elements on demand instead of materialising a new list per operation.

options.text: A sequence runs the work on multiple threads automatically
options.rationale: Sequences are lazy, not automatically parallel.

options.text: A sequence guarantees the data is sorted
options.rationale: Sequences do not sort unless you ask them to.

options.text: A sequence makes the collection mutable

items.explanation: Correct: sequences process elements on demand instead of materialising a new list per operation.
